city.Malawi.description: This friendly, landlocked country in southeastern Africa is famous for enormous Lake Malawi, which holds more kinds of fish than any other lake on Earth, and for the towering granite peak of Mount Mulanje.
city.Malawi.landmark: wooden sailing dhow on the crystal-clear turquoise water of Lake Malawi at sunset
city.Malawi.flag: black, red, and green stripes with a red rising sun in the top black stripe
city.Malawi.clue.0: kept talking about heading to a small, friendly country tucked into southeastern Africa
city.Malawi.clue.1: kept talking about a giant lake so full of tiny, brightly colored fish that no other lake has more kinds
city.Mauritania.description: This mostly desert country in Northwest Africa is covered by the sandy Sahara. It is known for the giant bullseye called the Eye of the Sahara and one of the longest trains in the world, which hauls iron ore to the coast.
city.Mauritania.landmark: vast concentric rings of the Richat Structure
city.Mauritania.greeting: In Arabic, people say hello with “As-salamu alaykum” (as-sa-LAAM a-LAY-koom), meaning “peace be upon you.”
city.Mauritania.flag: studied a flag in a guidebook: bright green with a golden crescent moon and star, and a red stripe at the top and bottom
city.Mauritania.clue.0: was dying to see a giant bullseye pressed into the sand, so big that astronauts can spot it from space
city.Mauritania.clue.1: wanted to ride one of the longest trains on Earth as it hauls heavy iron ore across the dunes
city.Mozambique.description: This long, coastal country in southeastern Africa stretches along the warm Indian Ocean. It is known for its coral reefs, gentle sea cows called dugongs, and a tiny historic island of Swahili and Portuguese buildings.
city.Mozambique.landmark: traditional dhow sailing past the white beaches and turquoise reefs of the Bazaruto Islands
city.Mozambique.flag: drew a flag with green, black, and yellow stripes, a red triangle, a yellow star, and a rifle
city.Mozambique.clue.0: asked about boats to a long, skinny coastal country in southeastern Africa
city.Mozambique.clue.1: planned to explore a tiny island packed with old Swahili and Portuguese buildings
city.Namibia.description: This Southern African country is known for the towering red dunes of the Namib — one of the oldest deserts on Earth — and a foggy Atlantic shore nicknamed the Skeleton Coast.
city.Namibia.greeting: The official language is actually English — but in Oshiwambo, spoken by many, hello is “Wa lala po” (wah-LAH-lah-poh).
city.Namibia.flag: sketched a flag with a red stripe cutting across and a golden sun in the corner
city.Namibia.clue.0: planned to climb some of the tallest sand dunes in the world, glowing red at sunrise
city.Namibia.clue.1: was curious about a foggy coast scattered with old shipwrecks
city.Niger.description: This large, very hot country in West Africa is mostly blanketed by the Sahara Desert. It is home to the last wild West African giraffes and desert sands hiding fossils of long-necked dinosaurs.
city.Niger.landmark: tall mud-brick minaret of the Grand Mosque of Agadez against the desert sky
city.Niger.greeting: French is the official language here — say hello with “Bonjour” (bohn-ZHOOR).
